eligible_but_not_contributing.note: ADAM VTE (NCT02585713) IS COUNTED IN THE INDEX CARD'S k=4 AND CONTRIBUTES NOTHING TO THE POOL, AND NOTHING ON THE PAGE SAYS SO. Its registered primary outcome is a RATE, not a count -- 'The rate (percentage) of patients experiencing major bleeding at 6 months' -- and the registry reports it as 0 per cent of 145 against 2.1 per cent of 142. There are no event counts to have. This review derives every per-trial effect from 2x2 counts, so the trial drops out in silence and k falls from 4 to 3 with no surface saying so. THIS IS THE SECOND TOPIC IN A ROW WITH THIS EXACT SHAPE: on DOAC_AF it was ROCKET AF. A count-derived pool silently excludes any trial whose registered primary is a rate, and the published k does not know it. SEPARATELY: the page carries publishedHR 0.26 (0.09-0.80) for this trial, which is a RECURRENT-VTE effect. Its registered primary is MAJOR BLEEDING. The number and the endpoint on this row are not the same endpoint.

outcome_definition_source.IDENTITY_CONFLICT: IDENTITY CONFLICT -- THE DATA AND THE REGISTRATION BELONG TO DIFFERENT TRIALS, AND THE REGISTRATION IS THE WRONG HALF. NCT02583191 is CONKO-011 / AIO-SUP-0115, sponsored by AIO-Studien-gGmbH in Germany, enrolment 246, whose REGISTERED PRIMARY OUTCOME is 'Patient-reported treatment satisfaction (convenience) with Rivaroxaban in the treatment of acute VTE in cancer patients in comparison with the standard treatment with low molecular weight heparin', measured from randomization to 4 weeks. IT IS NOT SELECT-D. SELECT-D is the UK trial of Young et al., and it is registered as ISRCTN86712308, not on ClinicalTrials.gov. EVERYTHING ELSE ON THIS ROW IS SELECT-D AND IS INTERNALLY COHERENT: the page's own record carries pmid 29746227, 'J Clin Oncol 2018; 36(20):2017-2023', and the verbatim sentence 'VTE recurrence at 6 months: 8 (7.9%) rivaroxaban vs 18 (17.6%) dalteparin (HR 0.43; 95% CI, 0.19 to 0.99)' -- and 8/101 = 7.9% and 18/102 = 17.6%, so the counts agree with the percentages they are quoted beside. THE TRIAL DATA IS RIGHT AND THE KEY IS WRONG. That is the MIRROR IMAGE of the defect this property exists for: PARACHUTE-HF was read as ANSWER-HF because a LABEL was accepted as identity, and the fix was to key on the registration. Here the label is correct and the REGISTRATION is not -- so keying on the registration, done mechanically, sends a reader to a German satisfaction study and makes every automated read of 'this trial's registered primary endpoint' return the wrong endpoint. Only reading BOTH catches it. NOT REPAIRED HERE. Re-keying to ISRCTN86712308 would put a non-ClinicalTrials.gov registration into an object where every other trial is an NCT, and the registry-read tooling speaks only ClinicalTrials.gov. That is a schema decision. PARKED.

primary.poolable_reason: THE THREE POOLED TRIALS DO NOT SHARE ONE ENDPOINT, AND ONE WHOLE COMPONENT IS PRESENT IN ONE AND ABSENT FROM THE OTHER TWO. Hokusai VTE-Cancer's registered primary, verbatim, is 'Number of Participants With Adjudicated Recurrent Venous Thromboembolism (VTE) OR MAJOR BLEEDING EVENT' at 12 months. CARAVAGGIO's is 'Recurrent Venous Thromboembolism' at 6 months, which its registry description defines as proximal DVT of the lower limbs, DVT of the upper limb, and PE -- NO BLEEDING COMPONENT. The row carrying SELECT-D's data is a recurrent-VTE effect at 6 months. So one trial's endpoint counts a HARM and the other two do not. THIS IS NOT A NEUTRAL MISMATCH AND ITS DIRECTION IS KNOWN. Edoxaban caused more major bleeding than dalteparin, so including bleeding moves Hokusai from a recurrent-VTE hazard ratio of 0.71 to a composite of 0.97 -- the registry's own Cox analysis gives 0.97 (0.696 to 1.359). Pooling it with two efficacy-only endpoints mixes a harm signal into an efficacy estimate AND DRAGS THE POOL TOWARD THE NULL. SEPARATELY AND SUFFICIENT ON ITS OWN: ONE OF THE THREE TRIALS IS MISIDENTIFIED BY REGISTRATION. NCT02583191 is CONKO-011 (AIO-Studien-gGmbH, Germany, enrolment 246), whose registered primary is patient-reported treatment satisfaction measured to 4 weeks. The data on that row is SELECT-D's. See identity_conflict on the trial. SEPARATELY AGAIN: THE PUBLISHED NUMBER IS NOT RECONSTRUCTABLE FROM ANYTHING THIS PAGE OR THIS OBJECT HOLDS. The index card served 'Published: HR 0.55 (0.30-1.00), k=4'. This object's pooled value is OR 0.7290 (0.4914 to 1.0817) at k=3. The page's own benchmark block holds 0.63 and 0.71 and no 0.55. Ten candidate pools of the page's own four published hazard ratios -- DerSimonian-Laird, REML and fixed-effect, each with Wald and Hartung-Knapp intervals, plus every three-trial subset -- give 0.60, 0.58, 0.64, 0.49, 0.54 and 0.75, and NONE gives 0.55 (0.30 to 1.00). The string '0.55' occurs on the page only inside CSS declarations and a chart legend position.

pooled.withdrawn_note: WHAT IS CONFIRMED, STATED AS PROMINENTLY AS WHAT IS WRONG. (1) HOKUSAI VTE-CANCER IS EXTRACTED CORRECTLY IN EVERY RESPECT. Its stored counts 67/522 and 71/524 are the registry's own primary-outcome counts exactly, and the page's hazard ratio 0.97 (0.70 to 1.36) is the registry's Cox analysis 0.97 (0.696 to 1.359). (2) CARAVAGGIO IS EXTRACTED CORRECTLY. Its stored counts 32/576 and 46/579 are the registry's own primary-outcome counts exactly. (3) THE SELECT-D ROW'S NUMBERS ARE INTERNALLY COHERENT AND CORRECT FOR SELECT-D: 8/101 = 7.9 per cent and 18/102 = 17.6 per cent, matching the percentages in the verbatim sentence quoted beside them. The trial data is right; only the registration key is wrong. (4) ARM ROLES AND ARM LABELS ARE CORRECT ON ALL THREE TRIALS -- edoxaban against dalteparin, rivaroxaban against low-molecular-weight heparin, apixaban against dalteparin -- and each label matches its registration's own arm titles. No arm is inverted here, which is worth saying because the two topics before this one both had inverted labels. WHAT THIS WITHDRAWAL DOES NOT ESTABLISH: NOT that direct oral anticoagulants and low-molecular-weight heparin cannot be compared in cancer-associated VTE, and NOT that these trials cannot be pooled. Three of the four register or report a recurrent-VTE endpoint and those are comparable. What cannot stand is THIS pool: one endpoint that counts bleeding averaged with two that do not, a misidentified registration, a fourth trial dropped in silence, and a headline reconstructable from nothing. THE REPLACEMENT QUESTION IS IDENTIFIED AND DELIBERATELY NOT TAKEN: pool RECURRENT VTE ONLY across all four, using Hokusai's recurrent-VTE hazard ratio rather than its composite. It is not taken because computing the ten candidate pools above meant computing that one too, so its answer is already known to whoever would choose the question -- the same rule that parked ABLATION_AF, SGLT2_CKD and DOAC_AF. It also cannot be done honestly until the NCT02583191 identity is resolved, because one of the four trials would be entering it under another trial's registration. PARKED.

primary.poolable_DEPRECATED_note: `poolable` MEANT ONLY 'the source page pooled these trials'. It was never a judgement that the pool was sound, and the renderer read it as permission to assert 'pooled on the X scale'. RENAMED to source_page_pooled, which is what it says. `poolable` is retained so nothing breaks, and it is DEPRECATED: read source_page_pooled for what the source did, and estimand_established for whether the pool is defensible. A PAGE SHOULD DISPLAY A POOLED ESTIMATE BECAUSE ITS ESTIMAND WAS ESTABLISHED, NOT BECAUSE SOMEONE ONCE POOLED IT.
primary.estimand_established_means: TRUE only where every contributing trial has been READ and shown to measure the same quantity, or the same construct with a variance stated. FALSE where that was checked and failed. NULL where it was never checked -- AN ABSENT ASSERTION AND A NEGATIVE ONE ARE DIFFERENT STATES and null is not a pass.
primary.estimand_established_does_not_cover_the_: READ THIS BESIDE `estimand_established`. That flag records that every contributing trial measures the SAME QUANTITY. It records NOTHING about what that quantity was measured AGAINST -- whether the comparators are of one kind, whether each comparison was randomised, whether it was concurrent. On attr-pn-review the flag is TRUE and correct while the pool combines patisiran against its own saline placebo, vutrisiran against PATISIRAN, and eplontersen against the placebo cohort of a DIFFERENT TRIAL. The two questions were never separated. Named as P48 in PAGE-STANDARD.md v1.21.0 and swept by scripts/audit_mixed_contrast_pools.py.
